title: An adjunction is determined by its unit, and by its counit
statement: Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be functors and let $(\eta,\varepsilon)$ and $(\eta',\varepsilon')$ be two adjunctions $F\dashv G$ (units $\eta,\eta':\mathrm{id}\to GF$, counits $\varepsilon,\varepsilon':FG\to\mathrm{id}$, each pair satisfying the triangle identities). If $\eta=\eta'$ then $\varepsilon=\varepsilon'$, and if $\varepsilon=\varepsilon'$ then $\eta=\eta'$; in either case the two adjunctions, and their hom bijections $a\mapsto G(a)\circ\eta_X$, coincide.

source.place: paragraph after Definition 0037 (definition-adjoint, line 3344): the bijection is beta = v(alpha) o eta (item 2) and alpha = epsilon o u(beta) (item 3), so it is determined by the unit, and by the counit
